title: On-Demand Vendor Asset Caching, Ultra-Lean Binary Footprint, Frontend Minification & Double-Gzip Fix
summary: Unbundles heavy vendor assets from the Go binary in favor of transparent on-demand CDN fetching and persistent local caching, introduces frontend bundle minification, resolves static asset double-compression, improves Mermaid export resolution, and streamlines native executable distribution.

categories.name: Binary Footprint & On-Demand Vendor Caching
items: Unbundle the bulky Mermaid diagram runtime from binary embedding, significantly slashing executable size while keeping memory usage minimal
Intelligent on-demand vendor caching: automatically downloads pinned Mermaid releases from CDN on first diagram render and stores them in ~/.px0/cache/vendor/
Serve cached vendor assets strictly from the same origin (/static/vendor/mermaid-12.0.0.min.js), preserving strict Content Security Policy ('self') and offline capabilities after initial fetch
Maintain native unpacked executable distribution to eliminate antivirus false positives and preserve OS read-only memory page sharing

categories.name: Performance & Build Optimizations
items: Minify the frontend client bundle using Bun (--minify), reducing uncompressed client JavaScript from ~448 KB down to ~250 KB
Add gzip bypass mechanism in static file handlers to prevent double gzip compression regressions on precompressed assets
Improve global export resolution in the Mermaid runtime loader for consistent diagram rendering across browser environments
Add cache-busting version identifiers to vendored Mermaid asset bundle requests to ensure reliable updates

categories.name: Cleanup & Testing
items: Remove obsolete re-exec helper routines (update_unix.go, update_windows.go) following the non-disruptive update notification model
Add unit test coverage for double-gzip bypass and update integration test harnesses
